extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, USPTO examiners, and appellate litigators (Federal Circuit audience)
extracted.subtask_short: ODP analysis with PTA and PTE
extracted.subtask_description: Legal standards for applying obviousness-type double patenting (ODP) and for deciding ex parte reexamination requests where patents have patent term adjustment (PTA) or patent term extension (PTE). Focused on how expiration dates, terminal disclaimers, and statutory provisions affect ODP determinations and substantial new question (SNQ) findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of obviousness-type double patenting (ODP)
rubrics_metrics.description: ODP 'is intended to prevent a patentee from obtaining a time-wise extension of patent for the same invention or an obvious modification thereof' and 'prevents an inventor from securing a second, later expiring patent for an invention covered by a patent that was filed at the same time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ODP applies where claims of a later-expiring patent are not patentably distinct from claims of an earlier-expiring, commonly owned patent. Terminal disclaimers are the usual remedy to overcome an ODP rejection. (Citations: In re Lonardo; AbbVie.)

rubrics_metrics.name: How to determine which patent is 'later-expiring' for ODP
rubrics_metrics.description: An ODP determination requires identifying which patent is the later-expiring patent, because ODP invalidates a later-expiring patent that claims an obvious variation of an earlier-expiring patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When patents have term adjustments/extensions (PTA or PTE), the appropriate expiration date to use must be determined (see separate metrics for PTA and PTE). The chosen expiration date controls which patent is 'later-expiring' and thus whether ODP applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: ODP analysis for patents with PTE (patent term extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a patent that has received PTE, 'ODP should be applied based on the expiration date ... before the PTE has been added.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows Merck and Novartis: a validly obtained PTE 'shall' run from the patent's expiration date (which may be adjusted under §154(b)), and Novartis held that a judge-made doctrine should not cut off a duly granted PTE. In practice, determine ODP using the pre-PTE expiration date (or the disclaimed date if a terminal disclaimer exists).

rubrics_metrics.name: ODP analysis for patents with PTA (patent term adjustment)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a patent that has received PTA, ODP must be based on the expiration date of the patent 'after the PTA has been added.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court held PTA and PTE are governed by different statutory frameworks and thus treated differently: §154(b)(2)(B) (disclaimed term limitation) and AbbVie support using the PTA-included expiration date for ODP. Thus include any duly granted PTA when determining later-expiring patents for ODP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory difference between PTA and PTE matters
rubrics_metrics.description: PTA and PTE are governed by different statutes (§154 for PTA and §156 for PTE) which have distinct provisions—e.g., §154(b)(2)(B) references terminal disclaimers but §156 does not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of these statutory differences the interaction of ODP with PTA differs from its interaction with PTE. Do not conflate the two frameworks even though both are statutorily authorized term adjustments/extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer as remedy and constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminal disclaimers (35 U.S.C. §253; 37 C.F.R. §1.321) are almost always filed to overcome an ODP rejection and can tie a later patent's term to the earlier patent's expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a terminal disclaimer has been filed, §154(b)(2)(B) prohibits adjustment under §154(b) beyond the disclaimed expiration date. Terminal disclaimers must be filed during prosecution (they cannot be retroactively filed after a patent expires to escape ODP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable concerns underlying ODP
rubrics_metrics.description: Equitable concerns informing ODP include '(1) preventing the receipt of an improper timewise extension of a patent term, and (2) preventing split ownership of related patents and subsequent potential harassment by multiple owners or assignees.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere presence of an unjust timewise extension or a risk of divided ownership is sufficient for ODP considerations; promises or declarations by a patentee (e.g., not to assign) do not negate those equitable concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question (SNQ) requirement for ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: An ex parte reexamination may be granted only if the requester raises a 'substantial new question of patentability' (SNQ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a SNQ exists is a factual determination reviewed for substantial evidence (In re Swanson). The existence of a SNQ is 'not precluded by the fact that a patent or printed publication was previously cited by or to the [USPTO].' Absent affirmative indication in the prosecution history that the examiner considered ODP, a reexamination request raising ODP can present a SNQ. Examiner knowledge of references or having issued ODP rejections in other proceedings is insufficient to show the examiner actually considered ODP for the challenged patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of review for Board decisions and issues here
rubrics_metrics.description: Board decisions may be set aside only if 'arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, unsupported by substantial evidence, or otherwise not in accordance with law.' ODP is a question of law reviewed de novo; whether a SNQ exists is a question of fact reviewed for substantial evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: In re Sullivan (standard for setting aside Board), In re Emert (ODP de novo), In re Swanson (SNQ substantial evidence). Apply appropriate deference depending on legal vs factual questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of finding ODP (scope of invalidation/remedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: If asserted claims of a later-expiring patent are obvious variations of an earlier patent's claims and no terminal disclaimer is filed, the later claims are unpatentable under ODP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-asserted claims that are not shown to be obvious variations remain entitled to their full statutory term, including PTA, unless separately found to be later-filed obvious variations. Invalidating only an 'adjustment period' would be tantamount to granting a retroactive terminal disclaimer and is improper if not raised and treated in the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver/forfeiture of arguments not raised before the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments not raised before the Board (e.g., seeking invalidation only of the PTA adjustment period rather than the entire patent term) are forfeited and cannot be raised for the first time on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants must raise issues before the Board to preserve them for appeal; the court will not consider novel remedies that would amount to retroactive terminal disclaimers if not preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's prior conduct does not preclude reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's prior awareness of related patents or his issuance of ODP rejections in other Cellect applications does not conclusively show the examiner considered ODP for the challenged patents during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To defeat a reexamination request on the ground that there is no SNQ, point to affirmative prosecution record evidence showing the issue was considered and decided by the examiner; mere knowledge or inaction is insufficient.
